jobs.title: Staff Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
About Us:

TRC, Member of WSP, is a global consulting environmental and engineering firm and one of the top design firms in the energy sector. Together, TRC and WSP’s 83,000 experts create positive, long-lasting impacts for our communities and our clients in the power and energy, transportation and infrastructure, environmental, and property and buildings sectors. As part of our team, you’ll discover a world of opportunities to connect with innovative thinkers, forge your path, and have fun tackling the world’s most challenging projects. At TRC, Member of WSP, you can have a rewarding career on every level.

TRC has long set the bar for clients who require more than just engineering, combining science with the latest technology to devise innovative solutions that stand the test of time. From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow-through of an industry leader.

We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications.

Overview:

TRC is seeking a motivated junior-level Environmental Scientist to join our Engineering, Construction, and Remediation practice in Concord, CA. The position focuses on a candidate seeking to develop technical skills to support various environmental consulting services.

This role will primarily assist with field inspections, documentation, reporting, coordination, and other compliance activities related to stormwater management programs. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of senior managers, integrate with our diverse regional team, and demonstrate flexibility and motivation to support various field and technical efforts.

  
Responsibilities:

* Conduct stormwater inspections at construction, industrial, and municipal sites.
* Assist with compliance evaluations related to stormwater permits and environmental regulations.
* Document field observations, site conditions, and potential compliance issues.
* Collect stormwater-related field data and support sampling activities.
* Prepare inspection reports, compliance documentation, and technical summaries.
* Maintain accurate records of inspections, corrective actions, and follow-up activities.
* Support development and implementation of Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs) and Linear Construction Activity Notifications (LCANs) and related compliance documents.
* Assist in identifying BMP recommendations and corrective actions and tracking resolution of deficiencies.
* Perform other compliance inspections, including Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) and tank inspections.
* Perform additional environmental field services and office-based tasks to assist with non-stormwater projects, including environmental investigations, remedial actions, construction monitoring, technical evaluations, compliance programs, and proposals.
* Perform environmental sampling (for soil, groundwater, surface water, sediment, soil gas, and indoor air) in accordance with state and federal regulations, QA/QC procedures, and established standard operating procedures.
* Coordinate with task and project managers, clients, contractors, and regulatory stakeholders as needed.
* Follow health, safety, and quality procedures during field and office work.

Qualifications:

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Geology, or a related field.
* 1-3 years of relevant experience in stormwater inspection/management, environmental consulting, or related areas.
* Ability to prepare clear and accurate field notes and reports.
* Responsibility and accountability to perform assigned tasks to completion, both independently and working with a team.
* Ability to learn through on-the-job experience and retain knowledge for progressive development.
* Strong problem-solving skills and written and verbal communication.
* Willingness to travel for fieldwork and project assignments (up to approximately 80% local travel). Field activities will require working outdoors in varying weather and site conditions and may include walking on uneven terrain and lifting light equipment.
* Valid driver’s license required.
* Must be able to pass a pre-employment background check, drug screen, physical, and motor vehicle records check.
* Prior experience related to stormwater, erosion and sediment control, field inspections, environmental compliance/permitting requirements, environmental sampling procedures, data analysis, and reporting.
* Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP) certification.
* OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER certification, including current annual refresher.

#LI-SE1

Benefits\*: TRC offers a competitive benefit package consisting of:

* Medical, dental, vision, and disability insurance.
* 401k package that includes both traditional and Roth IRA options and Company match.
* Paid time off contingent upon full time or part-time status and level of seniority (ranging from 15 to 25 days per year).
* All full-time employees enjoy a minimum of 8 Paid Holidays per year.
* TRC ensures that all employees, including those that work part-time, receive paid sick, family, and disability leave in accordance with the laws of their state of residence.
* These benefits are applicable to US employees depending on their employment status (full time, part time, or temporary). TRC offers jurisdiction specific benefit packages for International and Puerto Rico employees.

Compensation: In accordance with local law, the below salary range is applicable for the job and location associated with this requisition. Compensation will vary based upon experience, education, skill level, geographical location, and other compensable factors.

Other Compensation: Employee may be eligible for participation in the Company’s annual Discretionary Bonus Progra

jobs.description:

Together, TRC and WSP’s 83,000 experts create positive, long-lasting impacts for our communities and our clients in the power and energy, transportation and infrastructure, environmental, and property and buildings sectors. At TRC, Member of WSP, you can have a rewarding career on every level.

TRC has long set the bar for clients who require more than just engineering, combining science with the latest technology to devise innovative solutions that stand the test of time. From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow-through of an industry leader.

We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications.

Overview:

TRC is seeking a mid-level Geologist or Hydrogeologist to join our Engineering, Construction, and Remediation practice in Concord, CA. This career-oriented position requires providing clients all aspects of environmental consulting from proposal preparation to project execution.

The position focuses on a candidate seeking to continue the development of technical skills and management of projects, new and existing clients, and workloads.

The ideal candidate has experience executing field activities and drafting technical reports, as well as project or task management experience. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of senior managers integrate with our diverse regional team, and demonstrate motivation to serve and grow key projects in California.

Responsibilities:

* Coordination and execution of environmental investigations, remedial actions, compliance programs, and designs.
* Execution/oversight of environmental sampling (for soil, groundwater, surface water, sediment, soil gas, and indoor air) in accordance with state and federal regulations, QA/QC procedures, and established standard operating procedures.
* Evaluation of sample results, including development of supporting tables and figures.
* Site characterization and technical evaluations regarding sources, transport, and fate of soil and groundwater contamination.
* Preparation of technical reports, including documentation and summarization of field activities, data processing and analysis, drafting of soil boring and monitoring well construction logs, and development of conclusions and recommendations (including remedial options).
* Project planning and preparation, including agency coordination, permitting, preparation of site-specific health and safety plans, coordination of internal field staff, and procurement activities.
* Scheduling, field oversight, and management of subcontractors for utility location, drilling, excavation, waste disposal, etc.
* Coordination and execution of Phase I/II Environmental Site Assessments, Conceptual Remedial Action Plans, site closure reports, and other due diligence and site cleanup efforts.
* Regulatory compliance support, including risk assessment, monitoring, plan development, and corrective action implementation using working knowledge of EPA and DTSC regulations, RCRA, ASTM standards, and local, state, and federal regulations.
* Preparation of proposals for new and existing clients, including development of qualifications, technical approaches, and detailed cost estimates.
* Project management and administration, including responsibility for invoicing, direct interface with clients, internal and external QA/QC and safety compliance, and accountable management of scope, schedule, and budget.
* Implementation of TRC’s safety, quality, and project management programs in accordance with industry best practices and company policies.

Qualifications:

Required Education and Training:

* Bachelor’s degree or higher in geology, hydrogeology, or related field from an accredited university.
* 5 to 12 years of relevant experience.
* Working knowledge of environmental regulations (local/state/federal)
* Working knowledge of industry health and safety practices
* Experience with bedrock geology, including coring, logging, and developing cross-sections - desired
* Experience with aquifer test design/analysis, groundwater modeling, and/or 3D geologic modeling using programs such as Aqtesolv, MLU, MODFLOW, Leapfrog - desired

Required License or Certification:

* OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER certification, including current refresher training
* Valid California Driver's License
* Professional Geologist (PG) certification in the state of California, or Geologist in Training (GIT) with ability to obtain PG within approximately one year – desired

#LI-SE1

* Medical, dental, vision, and disability insurance.
* 401k package that includes both traditional and Roth IRA options and Company match.
* Paid time off contingent upon full time or part-time status and level of seniority (ranging from 15 to 25 days per year).
* All full-time employees enjoy a minimum of 8 Paid Holidays per year.
* TRC ensures that all employees, including those that work part-time, receive paid sick, family, and disability leave in accordance with the laws of their state of residence.

### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you interested in helping protect California’s vital water resources from future risk? The Delta Conveyance Project (DCP) is an essential climate adaptation strategy, as it protects against future water supply losses caused by climate change, sea level rise, and earthquakes, and has been described by Governor Newsom as one of the most important projects this state can advance.

If you enjoy digging into complex environmental documents, following a question through hundreds or even thousands of pages, and finding the passage that changes how a problem should be understood, this may be the position for you.

We are looking for a highly motivated, creative, detail-oriented, and adaptable team-player to join the DCP team of multi-disciplined environmental professionals responsible for providing a wide range of regulatory compliance and scientific services to support management of California's water resources. As a member of the Compliance, Permitting, and Mitigation (CPM) Unit, you will work on addressing some of the most complex and challenging environmental issues facing DWR and the State of California. You will be responsible for developing, reviewing, tracking, organizing, and monitoring draft documents; and assisting in the planning and coordination of DCP related activities.

### **Job Description and Duties**

Do you like working on complex issues, thinking out of the box, and learning new things? Would you like to influence water management to protect aquatic species and ecosystems? If so, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) is looking for a Senior Environmental Scientist Supervisor to lead implementation of the Water Storage Investment Program (WSIP). In this position, you will develop long-term, durable contracts to ensure the State receives the public ecosystem benefits to be provided by projects receiving funding under WSIP. These projects include new surface water reservoirs and groundwater storage projects. These contracts will administer public ecosystem benefits such as pulse flows for fish, water for wildlife areas, and habitat for species, and contain adaptive management plans to help ensure those ecosystem benefits are realized into the future. You will coordinate with CDFW regional staff, work directly with stakeholders and project proponents, collaborate with other state and federal agencies, and participate in contract negotiations. You will need to be able to interpret biological and hydraulic model outputs, understand fish and wildlife monitoring and management strategies, and understand water operations in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta and broader Central Valley. You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement.

**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. ### **Job Description and Duties**

This position offers an exciting opportunity to be part of a team of interdisciplinary professional scientists in the Aquatic Ecology Unit (AEU), working across a diverse range of field, laboratory, analytical, and research activities. AEU conducts innovative aquatic ecology research and long-term monitoring in the Yolo Bypass and Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta. The incumbent is responsible for leading the collection of fisheries, invertebrate, water quality, and other ecological data for the Yolo Bypass Fish Monitoring Program using gear such as a rotary screw trap, fyke trap, beach seines, plankton nets, and water quality instruments. The incumbent will lead field crews, operate boats and specialized sampling equipment, troubleshoot field challenges, and process chemical, biological, and molecular samples in the laboratory.

  

In addition to supporting long-term monitoring, the position will have opportunities to lead and contribute to novel research through special studies, from developing study plans and sampling approaches to analyzing data and communicating findings through technical reports, peer-reviewed publications, and presentations. This position requires adapting and modifying field methods to meet changing demands or situations, while maintaining high standards for safety, data quality, and permit compliance. The successful candidate will work closely with an interdisciplinary team of scientists to address complex aquatic resource management questions.

jobs.description:
**Company Description**

**Work with Us. Change the World.**

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**

We are seeking an experienced Team Manager to join our South East Queensland Water Resources team. We welcome candidates with either a Flood Engineering or Drainage Engineering background and approximately 15-20 years of industry experience.

This role combines technical excellence with team leadership. While your primary focus will be technical project delivery, client engagement, and business development, your time will be also dedicated to leading and developing a high-performing team.

About Us:

TRC, Member of WSP, is a global consulting environmental and engineering firm and one of the top design firms in the energy sector. Together, TRC and WSP’s 83,000 experts create positive, long-lasting impacts for our communities and our clients in the power and energy, transportation and infrastructure, environmental, and property and buildings sectors. As part of our team, you’ll discover a world of opportunities to connect with innovative thinkers, forge your path, and have fun tackling the world’s most challenging projects. At TRC, Member of WSP, you can have a rewarding career on every level.

TRC has long set the bar for clients who require more than just engineering, combining science with the latest technology to devise innovative solutions that stand the test of time. From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow-through of an industry leader.

We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications.

Overview:

TRC is seeking a motivated junior-level Environmental Scientist to join our Engineering, Construction, and Remediation practice in Concord, CA. The position focuses on a candidate seeking to develop technical skills to support various environmental consulting services.

This role will primarily assist with field inspections, documentation, reporting, coordination, and other compliance activities related to stormwater management programs. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of senior managers, integrate with our diverse regional team, and demonstrate flexibility and motivation to support various field and technical efforts.

  
Responsibilities:

* Conduct stormwater inspections at construction, industrial, and municipal sites.
* Assist with compliance evaluations related to stormwater permits and environmental regulations.
* Document field observations, site conditions, and potential compliance issues.
* Collect stormwater-related field data and support sampling activities.
* Prepare inspection reports, compliance documentation, and technical summaries.
* Maintain accurate records of inspections, corrective actions, and follow-up activities.
* Support development and implementation of Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs) and Linear Construction Activity Notifications (LCANs) and related compliance documents.
* Assist in identifying BMP recommendations and corrective actions and tracking resolution of deficiencies.
* Perform other compliance inspections, including Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) and tank inspections.
* Perform additional environmental field services and office-based tasks to assist with non-stormwater projects, including environmental investigations, remedial actions, construction monitoring, technical evaluations, compliance programs, and proposals.
* Perform environmental sampling (for soil, groundwater, surface water, sediment, soil gas, and indoor air) in accordance with state and federal regulations, QA/QC procedures, and established standard operating procedures.
* Coordinate with task and project managers, clients, contractors, and regulatory stakeholders as needed.
* Follow health, safety, and quality procedures during field and office work.

Qualifications:

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Geology, or a related field.
* 1-3 years of relevant experience in stormwater inspection/management, environmental consulting, or related areas.
* Ability to prepare clear and accurate field notes and reports.
* Responsibility and accountability to perform assigned tasks to completion, both independently and working with a team.
* Ability to learn through on-the-job experience and retain knowledge for progressive development.
* Strong problem-solving skills and written and verbal communication.
* Willingness to travel for fieldwork and project assignments (up to approximately 80% local travel). Field activities will require working outdoors in varying weather and site conditions and may include walking on uneven terrain and lifting light equipment.
* Valid driver’s license required.
* Must be able to pass a pre-employment background check, drug screen, physical, and motor vehicle records check.
* Prior experience related to stormwater, erosion and sediment control, field inspections, environmental compliance/permitting requirements, environmental sampling procedures, data analysis, and reporting.
* Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP) certification.
* OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER certification, including current annual refresher.

#LI-SE1

Benefits\*: TRC offers a competitive benefit package consisting of:

* Medical, dental, vision, and disability insurance.
* 401k package that includes both traditional and Roth IRA options and Company match.
* Paid time off contingent upon full time or part-time status and level of seniority (ranging from 15 to 25 days per year).
* All full-time employees enjoy a minimum of 8 Paid Holidays per year.
* TRC ensures that all employees, including those that work part-time, receive paid sick, family, and disability leave in accordance with the laws of their state of residence.
* These benefits are applicable to US employees depending on their employment status (full time, part time, or temporary). TRC offers jurisdiction specific benefit packages for International and Puerto Rico employees.

Compensation: In accordance with local law, the below salary range is applicable for the job and location associated with this requisition. Compensation will vary based upon experience, education, skill level, geographical location, and other compensable factors.

Other Compensation: Employee may be eligible for participation in the Company’s annual Discretionary Bonus Progra

Department of Water Resources

Fisheries Ecologist
  
ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,551.00 - $9,601.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **11/3/2026**

Electronic (Using your CalCareer Account)

By Mail

Drop-off

Print Job

Save Job

### **Job Description and Duties**

This position offers an exciting opportunity to be part of a team of interdisciplinary professional scientists in the Aquatic Ecology Unit (AEU), working across a diverse range of field, laboratory, analytical, and research activities. AEU conducts innovative aquatic ecology research and long-term monitoring in the Yolo Bypass and Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta. The incumbent is responsible for leading the collection of fisheries, invertebrate, water quality, and other ecological data for the Yolo Bypass Fish Monitoring Program using gear such as a rotary screw trap, fyke trap, beach seines, plankton nets, and water quality instruments. The incumbent will lead field crews, operate boats and specialized sampling equipment, troubleshoot field challenges, and process chemical, biological, and molecular samples in the laboratory.

  

In addition to supporting long-term monitoring, the position will have opportunities to lead and contribute to novel research through special studies, from developing study plans and sampling approaches to analyzing data and communicating findings through technical reports, peer-reviewed publications, and presentations. This position requires adapting and modifying field methods to meet changing demands or situations, while maintaining high standards for safety, data quality, and permit compliance. The successful candidate will work closely with an interdisciplinary team of scientists to address complex aquatic resource management questions.

  
  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Department Information**

**Division of Integrated Science and Engineering**

**Ecosystem Monitoring, Research, and Reporting Branch**

**Estuarine Science** **and Synthesis** **Section**

**Aquatic Ecology Unit**

**West Sacramento**

Department of Water Resources (DWR) was established in 1956 by the California State Legislature. We manage California’s water resources, systems, and infrastructure, including the State Water Project, in a responsible sustainable way.

At DWR, we are embedding climate change response into every project we undertake. We have set standards to help evaluate how each project incorporates climate resilience principles and ensure consistency across the Department. Our mission is to sustainably manage the water resources of California, in cooperation with other agencies, to benefit the state’s people and protect, restore, and enhance the natural and human environments.

DWR also strives to create a trusting and welcoming workplace where employees embrace diverse viewpoints and treat each other with civility and respect. An important component of DWR’s equal employment opportunity program centers around justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion.

Department Website: https://water.ca.gov/

Free virtual career consultation services including one-on-one DWR career consultations, application/resume review, tips for applying, and mock interviews, provided by DWR’s Recruitment and Workforce Planning section can now be scheduled via https://water.ca.gov/About/Careers.

### **Special Requirements**

Field sampling may require traversing uneven terrain and boat activities in rugged outdoor environments and inclement weather. Field sampling may occur on weekends and at night. The incumbent must be able to swim at least 50 yards and stay afloat for at least 10 minutes with assistance of a personal floatation device, work on boats without severe incapacitation due to seasickness, and transport equipment up to 50 pounds, with assistance. The incumbent will be required to drive to field study locations and to off-site meetings and must possess a valid driver’s license.

SROA and Surplus candidates are given priority; therefore, individuals with other eligibility may be considered in the event no SROA or Surplus candidates apply.
  
  
Applications will be screened and only the most qualified applicants will be selected to move forward in the selection process. Applicants must meet the Minimum Qualifications stated in the Classification Specification(s).
